reasoning: Minnie claims a 6:44 visit by the independently checked service clock, after the alcove locked at 6:38. Her claimed task involves an internal lamp that exists only in the superseded proposal, not the 6:31 installation photograph. Numerous innocent-looking accounts have one contradiction: several late visitors describe actual equipment, while several early visitors describe obsolete equipment. Minnie combines both, admits earlier salon business and has a payment dispute with Grant. Her Method speech carefully separates lighting from security, which fits someone exploiting an obsolete lighting cue as cover. It is the strongest accusation rather than direct physical proof.
experience: A fairer and more interesting comparison than a single impossible alibi. I changed my leading suspect after Opportunity and confirmed it after seeing the actual installation. The picture carried meaningful evidence instead of merely decorating a written clue.
confusing: My own IF INNOCENT speech claims a service-clock visit inside at 6:46, which is impossible. The briefing never explicitly tells me I am lying about my movements to protect my source. A real player may try to correct their box aloud or assume the game has an error.
The solution still ultimately behaves as a two-condition intersection. F4 and F5 announce that the records and personal clocks are independent, leaving little scope to dispute the documentary facts.
A lie about display work is evidence of dishonesty, not independent proof of poisoning. Coming Clean must explain why the obsolete installation was used as an invented cover story.
repetitive_text: Seven accounts repeat the concealment sentence beginning 'My other business that evening'.
Several early-visit accounts repeat 'Near the toast I was outside the enclosure ... dealing with my other business'.
accidental_giveaways: Minnie has a different ending specifically mentioning Grant’s salon while the other late visitors have the identical generic concealment ending. That editorial difference sharpened my Stage II suspicion before the decisive records arrived.
The case is readily solvable when all 16 testimony statements remain searchable in a single transcript; that is easier than listening to a crowded table.
improvements: Tell each innocent liar privately, in character, exactly what they are concealing and that their printed account is the cover story they should stick to until Coming Clean.
Vary every concealment sentence and the order of details. Give comparable salon admissions to several innocent guests; avoid a unique guilty sentence pattern.
Keep the actual photograph and superseded proposal available together at readable size so nobody must memorize a tiny image.
Have the host offer a short rereading window before ballots, without pointing out which categories to compare. Guests should control what they revisit.
Use a human rehearsal to measure difficulty; this transcript test measures logical solvability and editorial giveaways, not social recall.
limitations: Independent staged assessment of a scripted 16-character transcript, not a live interactive dinner. All three images were viewed. Stage I feedback was saved before reading Stage II; Stage II feedback was saved before reading Stage III.
